Both responses are correct. Each names chaining and open addressing, lists the probing variants, explains average O(1) versus worst-case O(n), and mentions load-factor-triggered resizing.

Word count matters here because the prompt says "under 120 words." By my count, A is about 131 words and B about 124. Both exceed the limit, but A overshoots by more.

On content, A adds the O(log n) tree bucket detail, the clustering note, and typical load-factor thresholds. B adds that lookups follow the same probe sequence, and that resizing is amortized O(1), which explains why resizing doesn't hurt performance. Neither addition clearly outweighs the other. B is tighter and closer to the constraint, so it has a slight edge.

Verdict: B
